action: Iris Ohyama account holders: change your password and change it anywhere else you used the same one, since the strength of the protection is not stated. Watch for emails or messages pretending to be from the company.
date_note: Reported in a Nov 6-12 roundup; exact disclosure day not confirmed
exec: A supplier breach affecting about 7.7 million customers, with password protection strength not disclosed.
plain: Japanese household goods maker Iris Ohyama said a break-in at an outside cloud service may have exposed personal data of about 7.7 million people, including account passwords that it says were encrypted.
summary: Iris Ohyama says unauthorised access to a third-party cloud service it used exposed personal data of about 7.7 million people, per a roundup relaying the company's disclosure; the company is still determining the full scope. Exposed data includes names, addresses, phone numbers, emails, gender, dates of birth and account passwords. The company says the passwords were encrypted but has not named the algorithm.
title: Iris Ohyama: cloud service breach affects about 7.7 million people
